question: Which operational records make a museum loan verifiable and recoverable?

documents.title: Object Identity
documents.full_text: The loan record binds every object to its accession number and catalog revision. Staff verify the mark before packing begins.

documents.title: Named Loan Approval
documents.full_text: A named curator approves the exact object list after reviewing the destination. The approval remains attached to the loan file.

documents.title: Condition Evidence
documents.full_text: A conservator records photographs and defects before transport. Return inspection compares the object with this retained condition evidence.

documents.title: Custody Handoffs
documents.full_text: Each custody transfer records the sender, receiver, time, and object identifier. Missing handoff evidence stops onward movement.

documents.title: Environmental Monitoring
documents.full_text: Calibrated sensors retain temperature and humidity measurements throughout the loan. Excursions remain visible in the object record.

documents.title: Packaging Seal
documents.full_text: The packing record identifies the crate and tamper seal used for each object. A broken seal triggers a documented inspection.

documents.title: Coverage Evidence
documents.full_text: The loan file retains the insurer, covered value, effective period, and exclusions. Dispatch waits until coverage matches the object list.

documents.title: Incident History
documents.full_text: Damage reports and failed checks are never replaced by a later clean photograph. Corrective actions stay linked to the affected object.

documents.title: Return Reconciliation
documents.full_text: Return staff reconcile every accession number and repeat the condition review. The loan closes only after discrepancies have named owners.

documents.title: Retained Audit Trail
documents.full_text: Raw approvals, custody receipts, sensor exports, and inspection results remain in one audit trail. A summary does not replace the underlying records.

documents.title: Watering Tomato Plants
documents.full_text: Tomato plants grow well with steady moisture and free draining soil. Water reaches the roots most effectively in the morning.

documents.title: Compost Ingredients
documents.full_text: A garden compost heap combines dry leaves with fresh plant material. Turning the pile adds oxygen for decomposition.

documents.title: Pollinator Planting
documents.full_text: Flowering garden plants support pollinators across the growing season. Several bloom periods provide a steady food source.

documents.title: Draining a Garden Path
documents.full_text: A compacted stone base improves drainage under a garden path. Edge restraints keep loose material away from nearby plants.

documents.title: Storing Garden Seed
documents.full_text: Dry garden seed keeps longer in a cool sealed container. A label records the plant variety and harvest year.
